content2.content: In Flutter, you don't just build UIs; you compose them. Widget composition is a core principle that involves combining smaller, simpler widgets to create more complex and sophisticated user interfaces.

content4.content: At its simplest, widget composition means that a widget can be made up of other widgets. A Row widget, for example, doesn't draw a row itself; it arranges a list of child widgets horizontally.

content5.content: Think of it as a tree structure:

content6.content:
MyScreen (Your custom widget)
└── Scaffold
    ├── AppBar
    │   └── Text("My App Title")
    └── Body
        └── Center
            └── Column
                ├── MyCustomButton(label: "Click Me")
                │   └── ElevatedButton
                │       └── Text("Click Me")
                └── MyCustomCard
                    └── Card
                        └── Column
                            ├── Image.network(...)
                            └── Text("Some description")

content7.content: Why is Composition Favored in Flutter?

content8.content:
Flexibility: Composition allows for greater flexibility.
Reusability: You can create small, focused widgets that do one thing well.
Readability & Maintainability: Well-composed widget trees are often easier to read.
Testability: Smaller, composed widgets are easier to test individually.
Performance: Flutter is optimized for deep widget trees.

content21.content: Widget composition is a cornerstone of Flutter development. By breaking down your UI into smaller, manageable, and reusable widgets, you can build complex applications that are easier to develop, understand, test, and maintain.
